sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Both are "has-a" relationships (UML associations), differing in ownership/lifecycle dependency.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: In **Composition**, the child object cannot exist independently of the parent — if the parent is destroyed, so is the child (strong "owns-a" relationship, e.g., House and Room). questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes method hiding in Java?

questions.question: Under the architectural guidelines of Dependency Injection, how should high-level operational modules interact with low-level data access modules?

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Method overloading means defining multiple methods in the same class with the same name but different parameter lists (number, type, or order of parameters)** — the compiler decides which version to call based on the arguments passed at the call site (compile-time/static binding).

questions.question: Why does the 'diamond problem' NOT occur with Java interfaces the same way it does with C++ multiple class inheritance?
questions.title: Why does the 'diamond problem' NOT occur with Java interface
options: Java requires explicit resolution of conflicting default methods instead of silently picking one
Java interfaces cannot have any methods at all
Java doesn't allow a class to implement more than one interface
Interfaces in Java automatically rename conflicting methods
questions.answer: Java requires explicit resolution of conflicting default methods instead of silently picking one

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: Since Java 8, interfaces can have default methods with bodies, reintroducing a diamond-like risk when a class implements two interfaces with the same default method.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **Java sidesteps ambiguity by forcing the implementing class to explicitly override the conflicting method (optionally calling a specific interface's version via `InterfaceName.super.method()`)** — the compiler flags an error instead of silently choosing one implementation, unlike C++'s implicit multiple inheritance ambiguity.
